Driven by population growth and tourism, urban expansion in Melaka Tengah has converted natural landscapes into built-up areas, escalating regional flood risks. This study evaluates flood susceptibility using a Geographic Information System (GIS) -based Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), assessing five core factors: land-use change, rainfall, drainage density, slope, and elevation. Results indicate a 6% increase in built-up areas from 2014 to 2023, with rainfall identified as the primary risk driver (31% weight).

Actinidia arguta possesses great commercial value as an economically important fruit crop, which accumulates abundant nutrients and bioactive components with medicinal potential. However, adverse abiotic environments, especially cold and drought stress, severely restrict its vegetative growth, reproductive development and fruit yield. Numerous studies have established MYB transcription factors as core regulators of plant abiotic stress adaptation.
